statement: The minimum number of real lines meeting four general real lines in P³ is zero.

source.location: Section 1, four-lines argument and Figure 1, printed p. 3; real quadratic-intersection consequence

scope: Four ordered real lines in P³ on the regular pairwise-skew locus; count distinct real common transversals.
notes:
Elementary consequence of the cited quadric construction: choose the fourth line disjoint from the real quadric. Such lines exist for a split real quadric and can be chosen skew to the first three. The derivation, not an additional numbered theorem in the source, establishes attainability.

For three pairwise-skew real lines, their unique containing smooth split quadric Q is defined over R. Common transversals form its other real ruling. A fourth real line cuts Q in two real points or a conjugate pair, and both cases occur on open sets.
